# Unsupported hyperlink child recovery

Generated by `tools/hyperlink_child_recovery_fixture.py` using Python's standard
library and the original XML/PNG helpers in `tools/image_recovery_fixture.py`.
No corpus artwork, reference application assets or third-party document engine is included.

`healthy.docx` has a mixed-format hyperlink containing a picture in each of the
body, a table cell, the header and the footer. Styles, numbering and custom page
dimensions surround these paragraphs. The other files keep that content intact:

- `leading.docx`: a paired permission range before the link's visible content.
- `trailing.docx`: a paired permission range after the visible content.
- `multiple.docx`: three paired permission ranges, before, between and after
  supported hyperlink children.
- `deleted.docx`: tracked deleted text before and after the visible content.

Relevant ECMA-376 Part 1 clauses: 17.16.22 (hyperlink), 17.13.7.1–2
(permission boundaries), and 17.13.5.14 (deleted run content). The sources pass
the repository's transitional schema checks. This recovery does not implement
permission enforcement or a revision-review UI. Its read-only final-content
view omits permission markers and deleted text; original package bytes remain
available for download.

At baseline `0856c98e`, all four unsupported variants lose all four linked
pictures. A rejected child rolls back the entire hyperlink. The fix uses the
existing visible-text projection at that child boundary, retaining supported
siblings, their formatting and their validated destination.

Unit tests check strict rejection, local recovery, link identity, picture
retention, formatting, package preservation and the export guard. Browser tests
compare every page's pixels and body/story geometry against the matched healthy
control at 100% and 75% zoom, block editing, and verify exact original downloads.
These are recovery controls, not a claim of native reference visual equivalence or full
support for the unsupported wrappers. Unsupported children containing artwork
can still lose that child's artwork in the text projection; failures inside a
recognized run or field envelope can still escape this boundary.
